Be overwhelmed by the complexity of glycoverse?

Imagine a package, performing all analysis you need, 
PCA, DEA, enrichment, or even advanced glycan derived trait analysis,
in just one line of code.

Try glysmith! Perform the comprehensive analysis pipeline with one function call.

## Installation

### Docker (recommended)

The Docker image includes R, glysmith, its optional analysis dependencies, the core
Glycoverse packages, and Pandoc for HTML reports. It supports Linux `amd64`
and `arm64` (including Apple Silicon) and is available on
[Docker Hub](https://hub.docker.com/r/fubin1999/glysmith) and
[GitHub Container Registry](https://github.com/glycoverse/glysmith/pkgs/container/glysmith).

Run these commands from your analysis directory to start an interactive R session.

```sh
docker pull fubin1999/glysmith:latest
docker run --rm -it \
  --mount "type=bind,source=$(pwd),target=/workspace" \
  fubin1999/glysmith:latest
```

At the R prompt, run `library(glysmith)`. Your files are available in
`/workspace`. To run a local script called `analysis.R` and save its outputs
in the same directory, run the following command from your terminal.

```sh
docker run --rm \
  --mount "type=bind,source=$(pwd),target=/workspace" \
  fubin1999/glysmith:latest Rscript analysis.R
```

For Linux file permissions, versioned tags, verification, and local builds,
see the [Docker guide](https://github.com/glycoverse/glysmith/blob/main/docker/README.md).

### Install in R

To use glysmith in an existing R environment, install it separately from the
[glycoverse meta-package](https://github.com/glycoverse/glycoverse).
Install the latest release from [r-universe](https://glycoverse.r-universe.dev/glysmith) with `pak`.

```r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::repo_add(glycoverse = "https://glycoverse.r-universe.dev")
pak::pkg_install("glysmith")
```

The latest release is also available from [GitHub](https://github.com/glycoverse/glysmith).

Install the latest releases of this package and its required Glycoverse
dependencies together from GitHub:

```r
pak::pkg_install(c(
  "glycoverse/glyrepr@*release",
  "glycoverse/glyexp@*release",
  "glycoverse/glysmith@*release"
))
```

To try unreleased changes, install the development version.

```r
pak::pkg_install("glycoverse/glysmith")
```

After installation, check the packages required by the default analysis blueprint.

```r
glysmith::check_glysmith_deps()
```

For troubleshooting, see the [glycoverse installation guide](https://github.com/glycoverse/glycoverse#installation).

## Example

```r
library(glyread)
library(glysmith)

exp <- read_pglyco3("pglyco3_result.txt", sample_info = "sample_info.csv")

# One line of code for the comprehensive analysis pipeline
result <- forge_analysis(exp)

# One line of code to save the results
quench_result(result, "path/to/save")

# One line of code to generate a report
polish_report(result, "report.html", open = FALSE)
```

After running the above `quench_result` line, you will get an organized result folder:

![](man/figures/result-folder.png)

Open `report.html` from your analysis directory in your browser.

![](man/figures/report.png)

*The report shown above was generated with `use_ai = TRUE`.*
